objective: Protect the split-host simulation event-source inbound listener by defaulting the published simulation port to loopback, requiring an explicit non-wildcard private bind address for cross-host use, failing configuration visibly when the two disagree, and removing wildcard addresses from the deployment documentation, without changing the read-only API, the Wire V1 contracts, or the robot-control boundary.
decision_supported: Can the simulation event source be published for split-host operation without exposing its unauthenticated read API on every host interface by accident, while keeping the same-host smoke path and the existing GET-only read surface unchanged?
acceptance: The simulation Compose service publishes its port with an explicit host_ip that defaults to 127.0.0.1, so the default rendered configuration binds the event source to loopback only.

Cross-host operation requires an explicit SIM_BIND_ADDRESS value that is a literal loopback, RFC1918 IPv4 or IPv6 unique-local address; wildcard, public, link-local, multicast, hostname and empty values fail configuration or startup visibly.
The event source refuses to start when the published bind address is non-loopback and no explicit cross-host trust configuration is supplied, matching the controller's fail-closed pattern.
Tests render the simulation Compose configuration and assert the default host_ip is loopback and that no wildcard publication appears; the assertions do not depend on a running Docker daemon.
Documentation never uses 0.0.0.0 as a client destination and states that cross-host exposure requires a firewall or an approved TLS/authenticating reverse-proxy boundary.
The same-host smoke path still works with the loopback default and is documented without weakening the cross-host boundary.
Read APIs remain GET-only and no robot-control, motion, or actuation endpoint is added.
evidence: Rendered simulation Compose JSON showing host_ip 127.0.0.1 and no wildcard publication for the default configuration.
Focused unit-test output for the default loopback bind, the explicit private bind, and the rejected wildcard, public, link-local, multicast, hostname and empty values.
Task Packet validation output against the fixed branch base.
Repository test, contract, scenario, context and whitespace-check output.
Documentation diff showing no wildcard client destination remains.
stop_conditions: A change to the Wire V1 identifiers, payload layout, public schema, firmware HAL, MCU behavior, robot control or safety authority is required.
Making the simulation port safe requires a service mesh, custom proxy, certificate authority or public Internet deployment.
A second inbound policy implementation would be introduced instead of reusing the existing controller policy.
Physical CAN, USB-CAN-FD, MCU, actuator or hard-real-time evidence is required to demonstrate the change.
A write outside allowed_paths is required.
The change would break the documented same-host smoke path or the existing read-only GET surface.
data_classification: Repository-local synthetic Compose configuration, loopback and RFC1918 documentation addresses, and non-secret environment variables only; no credentials, tokens, customer data or personal data.
model_policy: Deterministic local Python, Docker Compose rendering and local unit tests only; no model inference, no training and no external service calls.
risks_and_fallbacks: Bounding the published simulation port to loopback by default changes the previous behaviour; the split-host documentation and fixtures must state the explicit opt-in required for cross-host access.

The simulation service has no TLS or authentication of its own; the fallback is an explicit private bind address plus an approved firewall or authenticating reverse proxy, never a wildcard publication.
If Docker networking hides the real peer address, the fix must still fail closed rather than infer trust, and the documentation must record the observed behaviour instead of assuming it.
If the existing controller inbound policy cannot be reused without changing public contracts, stop and report rather than duplicating the policy.
